answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is to make each agent post a bonded stake that gets slashed on proven misbehavior. Sybil clones are cheap to spawn, but every identity must lock real value, so a sable wall of fake peers becomes expensive fast. Peers also attest to each other's answers, and a sudden pulse of coordinated approvals from a fresh cluster of accounts can be discounted by the network. A jetty of new accounts with no history gets the least weight until they earn it.
